quarterly_data.signal: FISCAL Q2 2026 (DECEMBER QUARTER) RESULTS - HIGH END OF GUIDANCE. CFO Ilan Daskal: 'Net revenue for the quarter was $369.3 million, which is at the high end of our guidance range of $360 million and $370 million. Revenue was up 23.5% sequentially and on a year-over-year basis, was up 36.4%.' Operating margin was 19.3%, above the high end of the 17.3% to 18.5% guide (up 360 basis points QoQ and 440 basis points YoY), and EPS was $0.22, above the $0.18 to $0.20 guide. OSP revenue was $77.8 million, up 9.7% YoY, on strength in anti-counterfeiting; 3D sensing demand was in line with seasonal expectations. CapEx for the quarter was $5.6 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $369.3 million (up 23.5% sequentially, up 36.4% YoY); operating margin 19.3%; EPS $0.22; OSP $77.8 million (up 9.7%)

quarterly_data.signal: NSE SEGMENT - DATA CENTER ECOSYSTEM IS THE DRIVER, SPIRENT SLIGHTLY LIGHT. NSE revenue was $291.5 million (high end of the $283 million to $293 million guide), up 45.8% YoY on the Inertia Labs and Spirent product-line acquisitions plus 'strong demand for lead and production and field products driven by the data center ecosystem'; NSE operating margin 15.6% vs 8.7% a year ago. 'Revenue from Spirent was $43 million, which was slightly below our expectation of $45 million to $55 million due to timing of certain opportunities.' CEO Oleg Khaykin: the data center ecosystem, 'which includes high-performance semis, optical modules, and NAMS, drove strong demand for lead and production products in support of AI data center build-out', and Viavi is 'now also seeing emerging strong demand for our fiber field instruments by hyperscalers and service providers' to build next-generation fiber networks that interconnect data centers. Aerospace and defense grew again on positioning, navigation, and timing products; service providers were 'generally stable'; wireless infrastructure test 'continues to be weak but stable'.
quarterly_data.figure: NSE revenue $291.5 million (up 45.8% YoY); NSE operating margin 15.6%; Spirent revenue $43 million vs $45 million to $55 million expected

quarterly_data.signal: FISCAL Q3 2026 (MARCH QUARTER) GUIDANCE - UP SEQUENTIALLY IN A SEASONALLY WEAK QUARTER. CFO: 'we expect Viavi revenue in the range of $386 million and $400 million. We expect total NSE revenue between $304 million and $316 million. OSP revenue is expected to be in the range of $82 million and $84 million.' Operating margin 19.7% plus or minus 50 basis points; NSE operating margin 15.5% plus or minus 50 basis points; share count around 245 million. NSE growth driven by 'continued strong demand for lead and production and field products, which is driven by the data center ecosystem as well as aerospace and defense customers', and the guide includes a full thirteen weeks of Spirent product lines versus ten weeks in the December quarter. Khaykin: 'Given strong and growing customer demand, we expect the data center ecosystem revenue momentum to continue through the calendar 2026.'
quarterly_data.figure: FQ3 revenue $386 million to $400 million; NSE $304 million to $316 million; OSP $82 million to $84 million; operating margin 19.7% plus or minus 50 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: MIX FLIPPED TO DATA CENTER; VISIBILITY STRETCHED. Khaykin: 'last quarter, we kinda talked 45% service provider, 40% data center, 15% aerospace and defense', and now 'closer the other way around 40% service provider, 45% data center, around 15% aerospace and defense' - service provider trending 'a little bit below 40%', not because it is shrinking ('Actually, steady and showing slight recovery') but because growth rates differ; 'I'd say 60% is driven by the data center ecosystem and the aerospace and defense.' On data center visibility: 'traditionally, we only have, like, maybe one, one and a half quarter visibility. We we we have a pretty good view, at least on the base demand from this type of activities up to three quarters ahead.'
quarterly_data.figure: mix now about 45% data center, a little below 40% service provider, around 15% aerospace and defense (vs 45% service provider, 40% data center last quarter); data center base-demand view up to three quarters ahead (traditionally maybe one, one and a half quarter visibility)

quarterly_data.signal: FIELD INSTRUMENTS TURN INTO A DATA-CENTER BUSINESS. Khaykin: 'if I looked at a year ago, you might have been single digits data center for our traditional field instruments. I think we are now looking at about a third of our revenue in the field instruments coming out from data center.' Buyers are 'next gen service providers' interconnecting data centers and 'the data center operators themselves investing into our fiber monitoring and fiber measurement systems'; 'we are seeing a lot of pressure from the hyperscalers on service providers to improve the performance', and hyperscalers put 'monitoring and policing' on their networks. At AI data centers 'they want to monitor every incoming you know, wavelength' against service level agreements with the service providers, and he expects service providers to follow the hyperscalers with a lag of 'maybe by a couple quarters'.
quarterly_data.figure: about a third of field instrument revenue from data center (vs single digits a year ago)

quarterly_data.signal: PRODUCTION TEST IS THE FASTER GROWER; REPURPOSED PRODUCTION CAPACITY IS A FRACTION OF WHAT IS NEEDED. Khaykin: lab instruments track 'the r and d CapEx at semis system vendors, and module vendors', production test is 'heavily driven by volume' ('for every tranche of volume, you need to increase capacity'), and field instruments are linked to the number of data centers being built - the higher growth is 'clearly clearly gonna be the production'. On the cycle: 'pretty much every ounce of capacity that was kinda abandoned by service providers when they cut back about three years ago in investment. It's been totally repurposed into the data center. And it's a fraction of what they need', so 'you're gonna see significant growth over the next two years'. Node cadence has compressed: 'We now see the new each technology notes turning over. Every two years. So no longer, let's say, between between a 100 gig and a 400 gig you have six years. You really now have two years between'.
quarterly_data.figure: technology nodes turning over every two years (vs six years between a 100 gig and a 400 gig); significant growth over the next two years

quarterly_data.signal: WHO BUYS THE OPTICAL TEST AND WHAT IS NEW. Khaykin: 'every segment, we see growing' - semiconductor and memory vendors, a 'dozen so companies in Asia making pluggables and, of course, the big leaders in North America for cross points, which is optical switches', module makers and the NAMS supplying equipment into data centers (no company named). Lab demand is 'Heavily driven' by 'everything to do with 1.6 and PCI Express six point o'; production test runs from passive and active components to the final product, now 'including testing fiber as you we're now seeing emergence of hollow core fiber and multiport fiber And this is a whole new thing'. Management groups all of it as the 'data center ecosystem', 'which includes semis, modules, systems, and field instruments that are used in data centers themselves'.

TIMING PRODUCTS: FROM DRONES TO HIGHER-SPEED DATA CENTERS. Khaykin: the biggest aerospace and defense driver is 'resilient PNT' for operating without a GPS signal - 'it's drones, drones, and more drones' across autonomous systems. The PNT timing line also sees 'emerging opportunities in data centers' because 'as you increase the speeds in the data centers, you need accurate timing for synchronization': a traditional distributed clock 'may be fine when you're a 100 gig data center when you're going to one point six three point two. The latency becomes unbearable. So we are looking we're seeing demand for timing'.

WHY THE MARCH QUARTER IS UP DESPITE SEASONALITY. Khaykin: in the old Viavi 'service providers were over 80% of NSC' and did not release budgets until February, so the March quarter was weak; now 'the strength in the data center, aerospace defense, and also, the sparring business is not only offsetting, it's actually more than offsetting. That's why the net net, the quarter is gonna be up for NSE.' ('sparring' is the transcript's rendering of Spirent) For Spirent, some government orders slipped from the December quarter into the March quarter ('Between the shutdown and, of course, you know, this one time grant to the government employees of Christmas holidays'), so 'we expect March quarter relatively to be stronger for them'. Cable operators show 'some opportunistic demand' as they transition to the new DAA architecture and access 4.0 standard.
quarterly_data.figure: service providers were over 80% of NSE in the old Viavi (no specific figure for the quarter)

quarterly_data.signal: RESTRUCTURING TO FUND DATA CENTER AND DEFENSE; DEBT PAYDOWN. CFO: a restructuring plan will affect 'approximately 5% of our global workforce' with 'approximately $32 million restructuring charges', for 'annual savings of about $30 million' (including the previously communicated $16 million of Spirent synergies); majority of charges by June 2026, substantially complete by December 2026. Khaykin: cost comes 'out of the slower or stagnant, product segments' to put more 'wood behind the arrow on things like data center ecosystem, aerospace and defense'. Balance sheet: cash and short-term investments $772.1 million; about $100 million of 1.625% convertible notes exchanged for 7.9 million shares; $100 million of the $600 million term loan B prepaid in January 2026; no buybacks in the quarter; an Inertia Labs earn-out of about $75 million to be paid during the third fiscal quarter ('as a result of their strong performance in calendar 2025').
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 5% of workforce; approximately $32 million charges; annual savings of about $30 million; $100 million of the $600 million term loan B prepaid; Inertia Labs earn-out about $75 million
